Review only · American English · October 9, 2026 · Round 7

Scientists’ profiles: deeper proofreading and consistency review

No profile text or renderer code has been changed. The previous round’s L001 was already applied and is excluded from the remaining findings. This corrected report uses American English and supersedes the British-English report. Your separate explicit degree and title rules are retained: PhD, DSc, MSc, MA, BSc, Dr, Prof, Mr, Mrs and Ms without periods.

Each row counts as one finding. Repeated occurrences of the same rule within a profile section are grouped in that row; recurring problems are also summarized below without being counted again. The 83 credential rows represent 83 affected visible labels, although they share two renderer mappings.

Severity: High — meaning, attribution or factual credibility is affected; Medium — a clear error or deviation from an explicit rule; Low — stylistic consistency or a more natural expression. Low-severity recommendations are not presented as factual errors.

Numbering: The retained L identifiers are unchanged from the superseded report, with gaps where British-only findings were withdrawn. V001–V098 are carried over; V099–V112 are new verification questions. Some carried items now have external evidence, but their factual text still awaits approval.

Consistency issuesLanguage findingsNeeds verificationCoverage checklistSources and verification scope

Rules used in this review

American prose uses organization, program, specialize, modeling, honor, defense, center, fiber, labor and orthopedics. Official names retain their established spelling. The earlier suggestions to convert these words to British forms have been withdrawn.

Degrees: PhD, DSc, MSc, MA and BSc, without full stops or internal spaces. Titles: Dr, Prof, Mr, Mrs and Ms without full stops. Academician remains spelled out and is capitalized before a name; no abbreviated Academician or clear pre-name capitalization violation was found. German Dr.-Ing. is a qualification name, not an ordinary courtesy-title abbreviation, and has not been silently converted. No change from a spelled-out foreign qualification to DSc or PhD is inferred.

American quotation punctuation and month–day–year dates are retained; the previous British-only punctuation and date findings have been withdrawn. Thousands separators for counts and sentence-case standalone headings without final colons remain low-severity consistency recommendations. Differences in the presence of optional sections are not errors by themselves.

Affected current text → Suggested text; uncertain wording remains pending verification. An insertion/deletion can be highlighted on only one side. Excerpts include context; overlapping changes in different rows should be combined if approved.

Consistency issues

Undotted displayed credentials

57 profiles display Ph.D.; 26 display Prof. Dr. Use PhD and Prof Dr. Both mappings originate in the shared renderer; a future change should target English output without unintentionally changing Azerbaijani presentation.

Section-heading punctuation

Natural wording and sentence structure

Prefer clear verbs and natural collocations over literal translations and repeated nominal phrases. Do not infer authorship, degree equivalence or institutional roles to repair an ambiguous sentence.

Washington university names

Use Washington University in St. Louis for Huseynli’s WashU affiliation. The University of Washington in Seattle is a different institution. The shortened heading and two conflicting biography mentions are covered by carried item V002, now supported by the official faculty page and CV.

George Washington University in profile 5 is a third, distinct university. Its directory confirms Mammadova’s GW association but raises questions about the stated rank and degree.

Names, institutions and titles requiring confirmation

Compare Messoud/Masud; Vehid Geruslu/Vahid Garousi/Garuslu; Sirajov/Siracov; Hankook/Hankuk; Bilkend/Bilkent; Qafqaz/Caucasus; Nuremberg/Erlangen name orders; Kharkov/Kharkiv; and the inconsistent World Fatwa organization names. All are retained as verification findings. Do not merge institutions just because their names resemble one another.

Honored and Center are valid American spellings. Official translated names still require confirmation where the institution or award identity is unclear. Generic job-title capitalization has been checked separately from formal names and title-case affiliation labels; inconsistent casing alone does not justify guessing official ranks.

2. Aytekin Huseynli

Ph.D. · USA · Social policy

Assistant Research Professor, Washington University (St. Louis)

Block 1 Aytekin Huseynli is an international specialist in social policy, social work, child and family welfare. Dr. Huseynli is an assistant professor at the University of Washington. Her applied research focuses on the formulation of social policies, especially the improvement of family and child welfare. Aytekin Huseynli also explores strategies and ways to channel natural resource revenues into social development in countries rich in oil, gas and minerals. Aytekin Huseynli's doctoral dissertation led to the creation of the National Children's Fund state program, which covers 7 million children in Kazakhstan and is financed by a portion of the oil and gas wealth.

Block 2 She is the author of 3 chapters in 3 books in the field of social policy, social work and social development, 15 scientific articles in 15 international scientific journals, and more than 20 publications, and she is a member of the editorial boards of 2 scientific journals in the field of social development, social policy and social work. She gave presentations at more than 20 international scientific conferences and received 2 international awards for her scientific work. She was the scientific supervisor of more than 10 students. Aytekin Huseynli teaches social research, statistics, program evaluation and social policy. Currently, she is the head of several research projects.

Block 3 A pioneer in her field, Aytekin Huseynli is one of the first professional social workers who received an education in the field of social work in the post-Soviet region and is one of the founders of the social work profession and education in Azerbaijan. Block 4 She is a member of the Board of Directors of the Global Program at the Brown School of the University of Washington, the deputy director of international programs at the Center for Social Development, and an associate professor at the Center for Child Abuse Research, Training and Education. Sources and verification scope

Checked on October 9, 2026. External verification focused on the required Washington distinction and selected concrete institutional conflicts. This is not a claim that every career fact or every foreign institution has been independently verified.

  • WashU Brown School — official Huseynli faculty profile and official CV: affiliation, displayed English name and rank.
  • GW — Mammadova directory, GW leadership and 2026 research-day list: GW association, role and qualification questions.
  • UTA — official keyboard faculty page: Javadova-Spitzberg’s institution, degree, rank and composer-name discrepancy.
  • Berkeley Lab — institutional publication: historical evidence for Joint Genome Institute; current affiliation is not established by a 2007 source.
  • EMBO — official name: Organization is retained inside the official name.

All source-file hashes were checked before and after this review. No source changes occurred. The HTML report has been structurally checked; browser visual preview was unavailable.

Completion: 83 profiles; 498 sections checked per pass; two complete passes; 463 biography blocks included. No profile text changed.
